messages:
maya (sec-eng): FYI trivy scan pipeline started failing intermittently on the scheduled run at 03:00 UTC — saw a bunch of suppression mismatches and a KMS decrypt error in the same window.
jon (infra): seeing that too. logs show 429s from GHAS API followed by `kms:Decrypt` failures for the scanner service account.
arun (eng-sre): hmm, 429 then KMS errors — could be a retry storm causing tokens to race. paste of relevant log:```
2024-06-15T03:01:12Z scanner-worker[pid=1412]: GET https://api.github.com/repos/org/repo/code-scanning 429 rate limit
2024-06-15T03:01:13Z scanner-worker[pid=1412]: trivy: apply-suppressions failed: lookup suppression-id: permission denied
2024-06-15T03:01:14Z scanner-worker[pid=1412]: aws-kms:Decrypt error: access denied for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123:key/abcd-efgh
```
liz (product-security): suppression mismatches usually mean the suppression store and the scan metadata diverged (e.g., suppression created for a package version but scan sees a different lockfile hash). Could be concurrent updates to suppression DB during the scan.
maya (sec-eng): I ran a quick diff against suppression manifests in S3 and the DB — noticed one suppression entry that had an extra `scope: manifest:sha256` field in S3 but not in DB. Might be a write-race during the suppression sync job.
jon (infra): suppression-sync job is scheduled on a cron in `scanner-ops` namespace — last deploy was yesterday with RBAC tweaks to let it read from the governance role. Did we change the service account permissions? @arun?
arun (eng-sre): we updated the RoleBinding to add `scanner-sync-sa` to `kms-decrypt` role last night. That was supposed to unblock on-prem audits. Possible we mis-scoped and the pod sometimes assumes a different IRSA role during bursts.
liz (product-security): Actionable: we need (1) triage the suppression divergence, (2) confirm RBAC/IRSA for scanner pods, (3) short-term mitigation to stop failing scheduled scans so customers aren't hit by flapping.
maya (sec-eng): CVEs involved in recent runs were mainly low/medium with a couple medium-high libs: CVE-2023-4975, CVE-2024-1102. Priority is to ensure scans complete reliably; we can postpone auto-fix PRs until we confirm suppression correctness.
arun (eng-sre): quick mitigation: pause scheduled scanner CronJob for 1 hour and run a one-off with lower concurrency to avoid bursts. Command: `kubectl patch cronjob scanner-cron -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' -n scanner-ops`
jon (infra): I'll patch RBAC to add explicit KMS decrypt policy to the scanner-sync role and pin the IRSA mapping so pods don't flip roles mid-burst. Will submit PR in 10m.
maya (sec-eng): for the suppression divergence: I can run a reconcile script that compares S3 JSON -> DB records and flags mismatches. Script output sample:```
MISMATCH: suppression_id=svc-4042 pkg=npm:left-pad expected_hash=sha256:aaa seen=sha256:bbb
```
liz (product-security): good. Also add an audit-log entry to the customer-facing tracker: "scheduled scans flapped 03:00 UTC; suppressions being reconciled; mitigations applied". Keep customers posted.
arun (eng-sre): PR  #382 created to pin IRSA and add KMS policy. Rolling update will happen after approval. I'll also reduce `maxConcurrentWorkers` in scanner config from 12->4 for the one-off.
jon (infra): after we confirm RBAC/KMS fix, we should backfill suppression-sync idempotency — add optimistic locking on manifest hash. I'll propose a small DB migration to add a `manifest_sha` column and update the sync worker to compare-and-set.
maya (sec-eng): owners: maya -> suppression reconcile script + run, arun -> patch/one-off run and concurrency reduction, jon -> RBAC PR + DB migration proposal, liz -> customer comms + CVE tracking.
liz (product-security): timeline? aiming to have scans stable in 2h and suppression reconcile done in 6h.
arun (eng-sre): started the one-off run in reduced concurrency at 03:25 UTC. early signs: fewer 429s and no new KMS denies so far.
scanner-bot: One-off run completed: 412 repos scanned, 18 suppression mismatches detected, 3 KMS decrypt errors during run (all for old key alias).
maya (sec-eng): the 3 KMS errors correspond to legacy key alias `alias/old-scanner-key` — looks like rotation didn't update some job config. I'll add a migration step to update any job env var referencing old alias.
jon (infra): merged RBAC PR and applied IRSA pin. rolling update done. watch for further 429s.
arun (eng-sre): monitors show rate of GHAS 429s back to baseline after scaling back concurrency. sched scans still suspended.
liz (product-security): I'll draft the customer blurb and post in #announcements once we confirm no further errors.
maya (sec-eng): follow-ups: suppression reconcile run (maya) — upload CSV to /reports/scanner/reconcile/1905123456.csv; DB migration proposal (jon) PR in 24h; job env alias sweep (maya) patch in the same PR as reconcile; add an automated check in CI to detect suppression manifest/DB mismatches (low effort).
jon (infra): noted. thanks team. :thumbsup:
